text: The segmentation model architecture has 2 independent output heads (crack and pothole).
Crack types are not classified into separate distress categories.
value: crack types are not classified into separate distress categories

text: Distress feature crack_area_frac measures the fraction of roadway surface covered by crack distress.
Distress feature crack_length_px measures pruned skeleton centerline length in pixels.
Distress feature crack_length_short_sides normalizes crack length by 512 px short sides.
Distress feature mean_width_px measures mean crack width in pixels.
Distress feature relative_width measures scale-invariant relative crack width.
Distress feature max_width_px measures maximum local crack diameter.
Distress feature width_p90_px measures the 90th percentile of crack width.
Distress feature n_crack_components counts distinct 8-connected crack components.
Distress feature n_junctions counts branching nodes on the pruned skeleton.
Distress feature cells counts enclosed background regions inside closed crack masks.
Distress feature network_index measures topological meshing density per 100 px.
Distress feature pothole_count counts distinct pothole defects.
Distress feature pothole_area_frac measures the fraction of surface occupied by potholes.
Distress feature largest_pothole_frac measures surface fraction of the largest pothole.
Deduct values are modeled as power-law functions: DV = min(100.0, a * q^b).
sPCI v1 parameters and engine are frozen under tag spci-v1-frozen pointing to commit 68a30aa.
sPCI is computed from corrected deduct values via CDV aggregation.
CRACK500 split has 329 train, 70 val, 72 test images (471 total).
road_crack split has 290 train, 77 val, 68 test images (435 total).
pothole split has 612 train, 108 val, 60 test images (780 total).
Combined segmentation dataset has 1,231 train, 255 val, 200 test images (1,686 total).
rdd2022es has 20,480 train, 2,560 val, 2,560 test images (25,600 total across 4 countries with 8 classes).
CRACK500 has 2.65% pixel-weighted foreground and 2.73% mean per-image foreground.
road_crack has 1.75% pixel-weighted foreground for Value 1 crack pixels.
pothole has 15.98% pixel-weighted foreground.
Double-blind human validation achieves 36.0/47 = 76.60% agreement with 1 labeler and 13 same pairs excluded.
Human test pairs totaled 60 (27 A, 20 B, 13 same).
On crack distress, human agreement is 30/33 = 90.91%.
On pothole distress, human agreement is 6.0/14 = 42.86%.
The paired difference vs the damage-area baseline is +2.13 percentage points with 95% CI [-2.13%, +7.45%], showing no detectable difference.
The 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the difference vs damage-area baseline is -2.13% to +7.45%.
On 800 clean zero-box RDD2022ES test images, crack flag > 0.1% occurs on 5.12% and pothole flag > 0.1% occurs on 45.62%.
On RDD2022ES test images with pothole boxes, the pothole channel hit rate is 19.29%.
On RDD2022ES test images with crack boxes, the crack channel hit rate is 8.48%.
On RDD2022ES test images with only crack boxes, false pothole detections > 0.1% occur on 34.12%.
Simulation costs, budgets, and expenditures are illustrative benchmark units, not real dollars.
Network geometry is drawn per pool, yielding 668,192.9 m2 on all vs 702,354.8 m2 on cracks, producing different annual budgets (334,096.5 vs 351,177.4 units).
On pool cracks, P1 spends only 1,629,136 units (46.39% of pool budget) because it ignores segments with PCI >= 40.
When budget does not bind (49.50% spent), P2 and P2t select the exact same segments.
